Let’s talk about something most folks rarely notice— the energy of life and how it flows within us. You know those moments when you suddenly feel a heaviness in your chest, or a knot in your stomach? That’s often your body’s way of telling you that something’s off, that the natural current inside you isn’t moving as it should.
This energy—the very current of life—usually flows through your heart and body without you even realizing it. When it’s moving freely, you feel alive, light, and at ease. But when something blocks it, that’s when discomfort and restlessness creep in.
Picture this: someone gets unexpected criticism. The words hit hard, and suddenly there’s a tightness in their chest. The mind starts spinning, replaying what happened, searching for answers—maybe trying to push the feeling away, distract, or rationalize it. But no matter what, the discomfort just doesn’t let go. Sometimes, it sticks around for days.
What’s really going on here? The energy inside has hit a roadblock. Out of self-protection, the heart closes itself off, and the flow gets interrupted. Over time, these little blockages add up—shaping how we feel, how we react, even how healthy we are. So many people carry a low buzz of tension, never realizing it’s just years of unprocessed experiences weighing them down.
Here’s something to pay attention to: freedom comes from noticing these blockages and letting them go. No fancy techniques are needed—just a willingness to feel what’s there, without judging or pushing it away. When sadness or anger rises up, try meeting it with gentle attention. Sure, the feeling might get stronger for a bit, but if you just let it move, it passes on its own. Your heart softens, and suddenly that heaviness lifts.
Maybe you remember a time you finally let yourself grieve something you’d been holding back. The tears came, the pain washed over you, but afterwards? There was a lightness, a sense of relief you hadn’t felt in ages. That’s the energy being released, finally allowed to move.
This isn’t a one-and-done thing. Life will keep bringing new experiences, and sometimes old wounds pop back up. But every time you let energy flow freely, your heart grows stronger and more resilient. Over time, you find it’s easier to let go of the past and live with a sense of lightness.
Most of us don’t realize just how much energy goes into resisting what is. When you stop fighting and let go of that resistance, all that energy is freed up—for creativity, for connecting with others, and for real joy. The journey isn’t about dodging pain, but about letting it move through you— trusting that your heart can handle whatever life brings.
